Title: How do we run it today?
Narration: Do you know how we currently run our salary cycle? Let's start with how it works today.
On-screen text: Do you know how we run our | SALARY CYCLE | today? | Let's start with how it works right now
Visual / animation: Oversized question over a faint year ring. SALARY CYCLE lit in the accent, on a plinth, with the sub-line beneath.

Title: The current cycle
Narration: Today, our cycle runs from January to December. 12 months, one cycle.
On-screen text: CURRENT SALARY CYCLE | JANUARY | DECEMBER | 12 MONTHS  ·  ONE CYCLE
Visual / animation: Year ring on the left counting twelve months, range plate and month rail on the right, JAN to DEC, playhead walking the year. The bottom timeline draws in here and runs for the next four scenes.

Title: How merit & bonus are set today
Narration: For merit, we rely on expected market movement, based on projected market and inflation trends. The salary market data becomes available around November. For bonus, we use estimated Company Performance KPIs, based on the information available by December.
On-screen text: HOW IT WORKS TODAY | MERIT | Expected Market Movement | BONUS | Estimated Company Performance KPIs | HSE | FINANCE | PERFORMANCE | COMPANY PERFORMANCE KPIs
Visual / animation: MERIT card with the forecast line, then the BONUS heading and the three KPI tiles (HSE, Finance, Performance) rolling up into COMPANY PERFORMANCE KPIs. The bottom timeline picks up the NOVEMBER and DECEMBER markers.

Title: THE CHANGE (hero)
Narration: Now, we're moving to a new cycle. From April, to March.
On-screen text: OLD SALARY CYCLE | NEW SALARY CYCLE | JAN → DEC | APR → MAR
Visual / animation: The hero moment. The ring spins three turns and lands on April while OLD drops away and NEW rises. Underneath, the same twelve months re-align from JAN-DEC into APR-MAR - months with far to travel lift over the ones that barely move.

Title: What the new timing gives us
Narration: That shift also changes when the information arrives. By January, actual Company Performance is available. And by February, actual market movement is available. This brings the salary cycle closer to market best practice, so decisions rest on more relevant, actual information.
On-screen text: WHAT THE NEW TIMING GIVES US | ACTUAL COMPANY PERFORMANCE | ACTUAL MARKET MOVEMENT | TODAY | NOV | DEC | ESTIMATED | NEW CYCLE | JAN | FEB | ACTUAL
Visual / animation: Forecast chart resolving from a projection into a measurement, two ticked claims beside it, and the small old-against-new timing comparison. The bottom timeline picks up JANUARY and FEBRUARY, now actual rather than estimated.

Title: April
Narration: Merit increases and promotions will take effect on April 1. That's where the cycle now begins.
On-screen text: APRIL | MERIT | PROMOTION | EFFECTIVE APRIL 1 | START OF THE NEW SALARY CYCLE
Visual / animation: APRIL at full size with MERIT and PROMOTION icons rising, and the EFFECTIVE APRIL 1 pill. The bottom timeline picks up the APRIL marker.

Title: March
Narration: And your bonus will be paid in the March payroll. March is the last month of the cycle.
On-screen text: MARCH | BONUS | MARCH PAYROLL | END OF THE NEW SALARY CYCLE
Visual / animation: Month rail running the new salary year and landing on MARCH, with the bonus icon and the MARCH PAYROLL chip. The bottom timeline picks up the MARCH marker, then retires.

Title: What does NOT change
Narration: Now, one thing that isn't changing. Your performance appraisal stays on the same schedule, and it'll still close in December.
On-screen text: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL | JAN → DEC | NO CHANGE | SALARY CYCLE | APR → MAR | NEW
Visual / animation: Two parallel rows: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL JAN-DEC with a tick and NO CHANGE, against SALARY CYCLE APR-MAR marked NEW.

Title: The implementation year
Narration: There's one more thing, and it happens only once. During the implementation year only, the merit calculation will cover 15 months instead of 12. As an illustrative example, if your merit increase is 5%, that's 5% divided by 12, which is 0.4167% a month. Multiply that by 15 months, and the equivalent becomes 6.25%. The merit percentage itself hasn't changed - only the number of months it covers.
On-screen text: IMPLEMENTATION YEAR ONLY | HAPPENS ONCE · NOT EVERY YEAR | 12 MONTHS | + 3 MONTHS | MONTH 13 | MONTH 14 | MONTH 15 | OVER 12 MONTHS | OVER 15 MONTHS | ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE | THE MERIT PERCENTAGE HAS NOT CHANGED — ONLY THE MONTHS IT COVERS | 5% | ÷ 12 | 0.4167% | PER MONTH | × 15 | 6.25%
Visual / animation: IMPLEMENTATION YEAR ONLY with the happens-once chip. Twelve solid month tiles plus three dashed ones numbered MONTH 13/14/15. Below, the ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE card builds 5% divided by 12 times 15 term by term, then strikes the 5% through and resolves it into 6.25%, each labelled with the period it covers.

Title: The visual summary
Narration: So - April to March. That's the one to remember.
Visual / animation: APRIL to MARCH over three markers - the frame to remember.
